title: Best Right to Be Forgotten Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare right to be forgotten and data removal services: data broker opt-outs, search result removal, ongoing monitoring, reports and support.
intro: Removing personal information from the internet can be complex and time-consuming. These specialized right to be forgotten tools help streamline data deletion requests, manage your digital footprint, and exercise your privacy rights effectively across multiple platforms.

products.name: DeleteMe
products.tagline: Paid service that removes your listings from people-search and data-broker sites
products.pricing: $129/year for one person; couple and family plans available
pros: Covers 750+ broker sites, per DeleteMe, many through custom removal requests
Quarterly privacy reports showing what was found and removed
Email, live chat and phone support
cons: Premium pricing compared to DIY options
US-focused service with limited international coverage

products.name: Kanary
products.tagline: Data removal that also covers search engines, social media and AI tools
pros: Covers search engines as well as data brokers; Advanced adds social media and AI tools
Monthly scans on Core; weekly or daily on Advanced
Web dashboard plus iPhone, iPad and Android apps
cons: Costs more than DeleteMe or OneRep's standard plans

products.name: OneRep
products.tagline: Automated data removal from people search sites
products.pricing: $8.33/month billed annually, or $14.95 month to month
pros: Covers 300+ people-search and data broker sites, per OneRep
cons: Non-public data brokers are only covered on the pricier Pro plans
Some manual follow-up may be needed

products.name: Privacy Bee
products.tagline: Data removal service covering people-search sites and data brokers
products.pricing: From about $8/month billed annually (Essentials); Pro about $16/month and Signature about $67/month, billed annually

verdict.summary: DeleteMe and Privacy Bee tie for the highest score on this page's six criteria (DeleteMe is listed first alphabetically). DeleteMe offers email, chat and phone support and a detailed report every quarter, but it can't remove search results directly. Privacy Bee covers 1,100+ brokers and asks search engines to remove results on its Pro plan and above, with monthly progress reports. Kanary is third: it covers search engines on every plan and sends monthly email reports, but its $250/year Core plan costs more than DeleteMe or OneRep. OneRep is fourth, with a low entry price ($8.33/month billed annually) and monthly reports that include screenshots.

pro_tips: Cut down what new brokers can find by keeping social profiles private and not giving out your address or phone number when you don't have to, while a paid service cleans up existing listings.
Document all your data removal requests with screenshots and correspondence - this helps if companies ignore your initial requests.
Use multiple services if budget allows, as different tools excel at different types of data removal and cover different sites.
Set up Google Alerts for your name to monitor when new personal information appears online, then act quickly to remove it.
Remember that right to be forgotten laws vary by jurisdiction - EU residents have stronger legal protections than US residents.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see results from right to be forgotten tools?
faqs.answer: Most services show initial results within 30-60 days, with full removal taking 3-6 months. How fast a company must answer depends on the law where you live: under the GDPR (EU and UK) it has one month, and under California's CCPA and similar state laws a covered business generally has 45 days. Where no such law applies, brokers remove listings voluntarily and timings vary.

faqs.question: Are these tools guaranteed to remove all my personal data?
faqs.answer: No tool can guarantee 100% removal: new sites appear constantly, and some brokers don't comply with requests. Each service's reports show which listings it has removed, so check those rather than relying on a headline success rate.

faqs.question: Do I need to use a paid service or can I do this myself?
faqs.answer: You can submit removal requests yourself for free, but it's time-consuming and requires ongoing monitoring. Paid services automate the process and handle hundreds of sites simultaneously.

faqs.question: Will my information reappear after being removed?
faqs.answer: Yes, data can reappear as brokers share information and new sources emerge. This is why ongoing monitoring services are important - they detect and remove reappearing data automatically.

faqs.question: Which right to be forgotten laws apply to me?
faqs.answer: EU residents are covered by GDPR's right to erasure. US residents rely on state laws like CCPA (California) and company policies. The strength of your legal protections depends on your location and the company's jurisdiction.
